Alex — thanks for the quick heads up and congrats on the campaign. We can absolutely help; below are two pragmatic paths so procurement can pick fast:

Option A — Emergency uplift (fastest)
- Temporary quota: bump from 50M -> 200M tokens for 72 hours.
- Pricing on uplift traffic: 0.060 USD per 1k tokens above committed volume for the uplift window.
- One-time goodwill credit: Redwood can apply a $12,500 credit to offset part of the expected overrun (applies against invoice for Sep).
- Daily spend cap: $6,000/day during the uplift window (safety throttle).
- True-up: full usage reconciliation at month end; overrun billed at uplift rate minus credit.
- Timeline: can enable within 1 business hour after DocuSign/PO confirmation.

Option B — Short commitment amendment (recommended if you expect more traffic after campaign)
- Temporary amendment to committed throughput: increase committed tokens to 150M for the remainder of Sep.
- Discounted overrun rate: 0.045 USD per 1k tokens for over-commit usage during Sep.
- One-time credit: $8,000 (smaller than A because of longer-term commit).
- Requires signed amendment (can be routed to procurement today), service enablement within 24 hours.

I attached a short quote and a simple mutual action plan that outlines timing, PO/Docusign links, and who signs. I've looped Marissa (sales lead) and Naomi (finance) for approval on the credit and daily-cap guardrail.

If Option A looks good, reply with PO number or say 'sign' and we'll send DocuSign and flip the switch.

-Jordan
